It's a scripted talk on a clock; no real audio.

YOUR JOB: make src/components/hero-demo/VideoFrame.tsx interactive and driven by that state. Edit ONLY that file. Other agents are editing TranscriptCard.tsx, ExtensionPopup.tsx and PlayerControls.tsx in parallel, and I'm editing HeroDemo.tsx and page.tsx — don't touch those or state.tsx. If you need something from state.tsx, don't change it; tell me in your report.

What it should do:
- Replace the fixed HERO_CAPTION with the live caption: show SCRIPT[current] when `captionsOn && showCaptions && current !== null`, revealing words progressively based on time since the line started (about 3 words/sec) so it looks like live captioning. Keep the existing per-word black caption background style (each word its own `bg-black/85` span, rounded first/last), but don't rely on the CSS `caption-word` entrance animation timing (it uses animation delays from load); a short fade-in for newly revealed words is fine. Keep the caption to at most 2 lines.
- Click anywhere on the video toggles play/pause (`togglePlaying`). Show a centered play glyph briefly / while paused (subtle, dark translucent circle). Make it a real `<button>` with an aria-label ("Pause video"/"Play video"), keyboard accessible, visible focus.
- The "Live captions" badge top-right: show it (red, pulsing dot) only when captionsOn; when off show a muted "Captions off" pill in ink-400.
- Progress bar at the bottom: width = time / DURATION (import DURATION). Clicking/dragging the bar seeks (`seek`). Make the hit area taller than the 3px bar (e.g. 12px invisible), and show elapsed time like "0:36" small on hover is optional. Use pointer events; no libraries.
- When paused, the speaker silhouette could dim slightly; keep motion subtle. Respect prefers-reduced-motion (no extra animations under reduce).
- Keep the existing visual design (aspect-video frame, spotlight SVG, ring, shadow) and sizes — it must still look like the current design at all widths.

Code style: TypeScript strict (noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on), "use client" stays, Tailwind classes, no new deps, no em dashes in any visible text. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` from apps/web. Do NOT start or restart a dev server (one is running on 127.0.0.1:3100 and I'll check visually). Report: what you changed, anything you wanted from state.tsx.

content.text:
`VideoFrame.tsx` is now interactive and runs off the shared demo state. Only that file changed, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes. I haven't looked at it in the browser, so the visual check is still yours.

**What it does now**
- **Live caption:** shows the current script line when captions are on and the CC overlay is showing. Words appear at about 3 per second from the moment the line starts. Each word keeps its own `bg-black/85` background, with rounded first and last words. New words get a 220ms fade using the existing `word-in` keyframes, and the fade is skipped under reduced motion. I removed `caption-word` and its delays from the caption.
- **Two-line limit:** the caption box is two lines tall and fills from the bottom. When a third line wraps in, the oldest line slides out of view at the top, like real rolling captions.
- **Play/pause:** a transparent full-frame `<button>` sits under the badge and caption (both ignore clicks). It's labelled "Pause video" or "Play video", and its focus ring is drawn inside the frame because `overflow-hidden` would cut off the global outline. A play icon in a dark see-through circle stays up while paused. On resume a pause icon shows for 650ms and fades out, except under reduced motion. While paused, the speaker silhouette dims to 60%.
- **Badge:** "Live captions" in red with the pulsing dot when captions are on, and a muted "Captions off" pill in `text-ink-400` when off.
- **Progress bar:** the width follows `time / DURATION`. The clickable area is 12px tall over the 3px bar, which grows to 5px on hover or focus. Clicking or dragging seeks, and a time label like "0:36" follows the pointer on hover.
- **Keyboard seeking (I added this):** the bar is also a focusable slider. Arrow keys jump 5s, Shift+arrow 10s, and Home/End go to the start or end. It has its own focus ring.

The caption overlay is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`), because reading out each word as it appears would be noisy. I'm assuming the transcript card is the accessible version of the text.

I didn't need anything from `state.tsx`.
